evidence.failure_reason: JavaScript-rendered SPA; crawler returned nav chrome plus the word 'Loading' only, no instructions text
evidence.searxng_unusable: http://127.0.0.1:8080/search returned only OpenAlex/Crossref records on 2 queries, no web-engine results; abandoned after 1 call and primary URLs fetched directly
evidence.verdict: PLAN COMPATIBLE with one hard constraint: the TMLR submission PDF must not cite or link the identified Preprints.org version (or the Zenodo/GitHub identifiers), per 'double blind of the TMLR submission itself must be maintained by not linking to another version that includes the authors' names'
evidence.q1_public_preprint_allowed: YES - 'It is acceptable for a submission to overlap with the author's previous work if it was shared at venues or tracks that are publicly declared, in writing, to be non-archival, such as workshops, or on preprint servers such as arXiv and bioRxiv.' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/editorial-policies.html); 'You can still submit, even if a preprint of your work already is available online somewhere (as long as it's not in official proceedings for some other publishing venue).' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/faq.html)
evidence.q2_must_not_link: YES - 'Authors are also allowed to upload their submissions to arXiv or other preprint servers at any time, either anonymously or including their identity, though double blind of the TMLR submission itself must be maintained by not linking to another version that includes the authors' names.' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/author-guide.html)
evidence.q3_arxiv_required: NO - arXiv appears only as permission ('allowed to upload ... at any time') and as an indexing suggestion ('consider posting your paper to arXiv', https://jmlr.org/tmlr/faq.html). The only stated profile prerequisite is 'All authors must have complete and active OpenReview profiles' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/author-guide.html). No arXiv endorsement is required.
evidence.q4_anonymity: At submission: 'TMLR uses a double blind review process and submissions must be anonymized.' and 'Like submissions, supplementary material must be anonymized.' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/author-guide.html). Only the AE and EiCs see names during review (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/faq.html). Paper becomes public but stays anonymous during review. After acceptance identity is disclosed: 'Such information will not be disclosed to the reviewers, but will be once a decision on the manuscript has been made.' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/author-guide.html).
evidence.q5_ai_disclosure: REQUIRED - prior unit's 'TMLR silent' finding is WRONG. FAQ: 'Additionally, transparency is always good, so we also require that authors mention explicitly in their submission that they have used this tool, as a footnote on the first page.' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/faq.html). Corroborated by the 'LLM use policy for authors' section: 'LLMs may be used as general-purpose assistive tools ... LLMs are not eligible for authorship.' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/editorial-policies.html)
evidence.q6_stylefile: MANDATORY - 'The Author Guidelines page contains a LaTeX stylefile and template; these are mandatory. Any changes to the stylefile or template that alters the formatting, font, or layout of the manuscript may result in rejection without review.' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/submissions.html). Obtained from https://github.com/JmlrOrg/tmlr-style-file (zip: https://github.com/JmlrOrg/tmlr-style-file/archive/refs/heads/main.zip); repo contains tmlr.sty, tmlr.bst, main.tex, main.bib, math_commands.tex, fancyhdr.sty. Portal accepts a PDF manuscript ('Submissions must be PDF files generated using the TMLR LaTeX stylefile and template') plus up to 100MB supplementary in PDF or ZIP; LaTeX source is not requested.
evidence.q7_timeline_decisions: 'in general the rolling review process aims to deliver a final decision approximately 9 weeks after submission' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/faq.html). Three decision options only: 'Accept as is', 'Accept with minor revision', 'Reject' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/editorial-policies.html). There is NO 'major revision' option. AE assigned within a week; reviews due in 2 weeks (<=12 pages) or 4 weeks (>12 pages); discussion phase 2-4 weeks.
evidence.q8_code_data: NOT REQUIRED - 'We encourage authors to, whenever possible, upload materials that improve reproducibility. Specifically, it is suggested that authors submit supplementary material including data or code towards this end.' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/author-guide.html); 'Code and videos may be uploaded and associated with camera ready papers.' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/faq.html). Binding constraint is anonymity: anything supplied at submission time must be anonymized.
evidence.q9_parallel_review: PROHIBITED if the other venue is archival and peer-reviewed - 'There should not be any reuse of written text, figures or results between the submitted paper and any paper which has been published, accepted for publication, or submitted in parallel at another archival, peer-reviewed venue.' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/editorial-policies.html). A Preprints.org posting is public disclosure, not parallel review, and is the permitted kind.
extra_findings: Survey ban: 'As of September 1, 2026, TMLR no longer considers survey papers for review.' (https://jmlr.org/tmlr/faq.html)
Author quotas: Generalized Harmonic Quota Rule, N_1 = 2 and N_9 = 9, doubled for reviewers/AEs; desk rejections still spend budget.
No author changes after submission, no exceptions.
Licence: 'All TMLR submissions, from the time of submission to final publication, are licensed under CC BY 4.0. At all times, copyright is retained by the authors.'
Home page line 'TMLR does not accept submissions that have any overlap with previously published work' must be read with the Dual Submissions carve-out, not alone.
not_verified: OpenReview submission form fields (JS-only page): exact required declarations and upload widget file types.
Preprints.org is never named by TMLR; coverage is by category via 'such as arXiv and bioRxiv' / 'or other preprint servers'.
Whether a Zenodo data DOI counts as 'another version that includes the authors' names' - the rule says 'another version'; cautious reading applied.
Whether TMLR screens submissions against preprint servers for de-anonymization (reviewers are only asked not to search).

blocker: None for the nine questions - all were answered from TMLR primary sources. One item could not be verified: the OpenReview TMLR venue page (https://openreview.net/group?id=TMLR) is JavaScript-rendered and returned no instructions text, so the submission form's exact fields and required declarations remain unconfirmed.
next_unit_hint: Two follow-ups. (1) The prior unit's claim that TMLR is silent on AI-use disclosure is refuted by the FAQ footnote requirement - propagate the correction to whatever artifact carried it, and ensure the TMLR PDF gets a page-1 LLM-use footnote. (2) For the publication-order plan, the actionable rule is: build the TMLR PDF from tmlr.sty with no Preprints.org DOI, no Zenodo DOI and no GitHub URL in the submission version; reference an anonymized mirror if code/data must be reachable at review time, then restore the real links at camera-ready. A verifier could confirm the reviewer-side no-de-anonymization rule at https://jmlr.org/tmlr/reviewer-guide.html (not fetched, budget) and re-fetch the four policy pages to check for drift before any actual submission.
